issues.legal_issue: A defendant should be given a conditional opportunity to contest an ex parte decree on the merits where the proceedings were transferred without notice after the defendant’s request to engage counsel was rejected, despite the defendant’s later notice of execution proceedings.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance and mandatory relief concerning property the defendant said was his residence and the subject of a loan transaction.
The defendant applied to engage an advocate before the suit proceeded ex parte, but the application was rejected.
The suit was transferred to another court without notice to the defendant and was later decreed ex parte.

The defendant received notice of the execution proceedings before the date on which he later claimed to have learned of the decree; the property had also been conveyed to the plaintiff through execution.
The defendant offered to reimburse the expenses incurred in obtaining the conveyance.
The trial court allowed the application to set aside the ex parte decree, but the High Court reversed that order in revision.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and the High Court’s order was set aside, subject to the defendant depositing the expenses incurred to obtain the conveyance and costs. On compliance, the defendant could contest the suit, the conveyance would stand set aside, and the trial court was directed to decide the suit expeditiously. If the deposits were not made, the appeal would stand dismissed and the High Court’s order would remain in force.
issues.legal_principle: Litigation should, as far as possible, be decided on the merits rather than terminated by default. Applying the court’s discretion in the context of Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and noting the absence of transfer notice contemplated by Rule 89A, the Court granted an opportunity to contest the suit on terms that addressed the consequences of execution. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_revision_affecting_ex_parte_relief and request_to_appear_with_counsel_was_rejected and case_transfer_notice_was_omitted and execution_notice_preceded_claimed_discovery and specific_performance_dispute_involved_home and defendant_offered_reimbursement

predicates.appeal_from_revision_affecting_ex_parte_: The matter is an appeal from a revisional decision concerning whether an ex parte decree may be reopened.
predicates.request_to_appear_with_counsel_was_rejec: The defendant asked to engage counsel before the case proceeded ex parte, and the court rejected that request.
predicates.case_transfer_notice_was_omitted: The case was transferred to another court without notice to the defendant.
predicates.execution_notice_preceded_claimed_discov: The defendant received notice of execution proceedings before the later date on which the defendant claimed to have learned of the decree.
predicates.specific_performance_dispute_involved_ho: The specific-performance dispute concerned property the defendant said was the defendant’s home.
predicates.defendant_offered_reimbursement: The defendant offered to repay expenses incurred by the other side in obtaining a conveyance through execution.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning ex parte relief involves the stated procedural circumstances and the defendant offers reimbursement in a home-related specific-performance dispute, the output is a conditional opportunity to contest the case.
